record.oneLiner: A small feathered oviraptorid, famously misjudged as an egg-thief.
record.description: Oviraptor was a small, feathered oviraptorid from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia, 1.6–2 m long, with a toothless beak and probably a head crest. It was named 'egg thief' because its first skeleton was found atop a nest of eggs — later shown to be its own nest, which it was brooding, not raiding.

notableFacts.text: 'Egg thief' is a misnomer — the eggs it was found with were its own.
Later oviraptorid finds show these dinosaurs brooded their nests like birds.
Had a toothless beak and probably a head crest.
